chapter: New York, church bands and early training
title: Studying cornet with Mikell, then sent for by his sister in New York
summary: After losing his parents he was sent for by his older sister in New York; he had already studied snare, cornet and peck horn with Mikell from about age twelve, playing concert music and folk songs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well, let's go back a little bit here.
I want to get some of this early stuff down here before we get too
How did you then get into music. How did you start playing?
Well, I tell you, it was when I went up to New York. I explained that my sister, Mrs. Edith Inez Briggs Hall--
Was housekeeping with a lady by the name of Mrs. Spooner.
But you had started studying in Charleston, right?
Oh yes, oh, yes, I'd studied with Mr. Mikell.
And how did that happen to work. You just decided you wanted to play something and --
No, my sister sent for me.
I had lost my parents, you see.
Died, yes. And my sister sent for me, my older sister sent for me to come out there.
But you had been studying before your parents died?
Snares were first. Then cor-net after. Cor-net and peck horn.
And how old were you then, at that time?
And that is -- you were just studying straight concert music? I guess there wasn't any jazz yet at that time.
I played straight concert music, and folk songs, and you know --
